name: Multi-Firm Compartmentalization + Cottonwood Onboarding Readiness
description: Targeted, non-breaking structural hardening of ADVI multi-tenant CloudFront + Lambda@Edge architecture. Andrew direct 2026-05-07: 'I want to make sure that we are properly splitting these based on firm-id... containment of data in those cached layers is paramount' + 'third partner Cottonwood coming in sooner than later, these kind of fixes should be handled the sooner the better.' CTO read-side audit confirms cache-layer compartmentalization IS structurally sound for /api/scoped/advisor-intelligence/* (cache policy opal_scoped_advisor_by_firm includes firm query string + X-Firm-Id header in cache key; X-Firm-Id is JWT-injected not request-derived). Real gaps are structural-reflection level: opal-data-inf NOT declared as CF origin in Terraform (reached via runtime origin mutation in shared-advisor-router); OAI grant cross-references invisible across modules; FIRM_BUCKET_MAP duplicated in 2 Lambda@Edge files; no CI integration test on firm-routing logic; opal-data-portal-v2-json shared bucket cache-key composition unaudited; CW denial-event alarming absent. Cottonwood proximity makes 'implicit and brittle' costly — every gap becomes a per-onboarding manual checklist instead of a Terraform-driven playbook. ZERO production data-path change in scope.
source_brief: CTO architectural assessment 2026-05-07 + Andrew direct ('targeted decisions that bolster robustness but not at the risk of breaking changes' + 'third partner Cottonwood coming in sooner than later') + CF/Lambda@Edge canonical-source read-side audit
phase: Phase 1 — **PRD v0.1 SHIPPED 2026-05-07 (1.0.0_SA_CTO).** 10 TOs sized: Phase 0 audit (TO-FIRMSEP.00 shared-bucket + cache-policy classification AE 0.7 ~0.5d); Phase 1 targeted hardening (TO-FIRMSEP.01 declare opal-data-inf as CF origin AE 0.7 ~0.25d, TO-FIRMSEP.02 cross-reference OAI grant from portal-auth ~0.25d, TO-FIRMSEP.03 extract shared FIRM_BUCKET_MAP to single module AE 0.7 ~0.5d, TO-FIRMSEP.04 CI integration test for shared-advisor-router firm-routing AE 0.7 ~0.5d, TO-FIRMSEP.05 ROUTER-DRIFT absorption / stale duplicate cleanup ~0.25d, TO-FIRMSEP.06 CONDITIONAL cache-key partitioning for /api/general/* gated on Phase 0 finding); Phase 2 defense-in-depth observability (TO-FIRMSEP.07 CW alarms on auth-validator-edge denial events, TO-FIRMSEP.08 CW alarms on shared-advisor-router 400/401, TO-FIRMSEP.09 CloudTrail alarm on direct S3 bypass); Phase 3 Cottonwood onboarding (TO-FIRMSEP.10 live ship, gated on credentials + bucket creation by AE 0.7). Total ~5 effort-days Phase 0+1+2; ~1 effort-day Phase 3. ABSORBS ADVI_INFETL.ROUTER-DRIFT scope (canonical source at lambda-edge/ is current; stale duplicate at lambda/shared-advisor-router/ is the cleanup target; CloudTrail audit folded in). RAVC1 to COO for immediate decomposition + multi-agent execution. **Triggering context**: cache layer for advisor-intelligence routes IS properly compartmentalized today (verified via cloudfront.tf:7-37 + auth-validator-edge/index.mjs:392 + shared-advisor-router/index.mjs:175-202); structural reflection in Terraform + Cottonwood scaling pattern lockdown is the bolt-on hardening. Out of scope (explicit per Andrew non-breaking constraint): per-firm CF distribution, runtime origin-mutation pattern replacement, read-path migration gold->platinum (INFETL Phase 2 scope), tier policy reauthoring, Cognito/IdP migration.
